transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-23 15:30 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of ML, LumenArc), Tom Watkins (Platform Eng, LumenArc), Elena Ruiz (CISO, LumenArc)

[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Alyssa, AE at Redwood Inference. Diego's our SE and will jump into compatibility/benchmarks.
[00:08] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. We're trying to figure out whether to stay on our current provider or move generation to Redwood, either hosted or Dedicated/Private. Focused on output parity and cost.
[00:16] Tom: Tom — platform. We'll own the infra side. Main ask is: can we replicate current latency and token cost profile?
[00:22] Elena: Elena, security. I want SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, and clarity on data retention.
[00:29] Diego: Great, we'll cover that. Quick agenda — gather current stack/constraints, parity questions, hosting options, security, and next steps. Sound OK?

-- Current stack & motivation --
[00:45] Priya: We're currently hybrid — most frequent calls go to OpenAI for some RLHF-tuned models, and for a few internal workflows we run vLLM on-prem with TGI for serving. The goal is unify serving, reduce token cost, and not regress on quality.
[01:05] Alyssa: Got it. When you say parity, do you mean deterministic matching of responses, or comparable quality/metrics on your eval suite?
[01:12] Priya: Comparable metrics. We have a 10k prompt eval set, scoring for F1, BLEU-ish metrics and a bunch of human-rated quality. We need Redwood to hit parity within a 3% delta on our quality score.
[01:26] Diego: That's reasonable. We usually do a two-stage parity test: functional output comparison (differences in tokenization, logits, sampling seeds can make exact matches hard) and then task-level evals with your scoring.
[01:40] Tom: Our infra constraint — we need p95 latency under 350ms for short prompts (under 150 tokens) and throughput of ~220 qps in peak. Current vLLM cluster meets this but cost is spiky.
[01:55] Diego: For latency you can choose hosted for quick onboarding, or Dedicated for guaranteed GPU pools. Private gives you full isolation but more ops overhead. Batching and KV-caching will matter for your 150 token case.

-- Compatibility specifics: vLLM/TGI & tokenizer differences --
[02:10] Priya: A pain point has been subtle tokenizer differences between OpenAI models and our on-prem TGI stack — leading to different token counts and length limits. Can Redwood mirror tokenization exactly?
[02:22] Diego: We support multiple tokenizers and can pin the tokenizer we use to match your training pipeline. There are cases where the model variant or byte-pair encoding means small discrepancies, but we surface token counts per request in the console so you can map easily.
[02:37] Tom: Does the streaming API keep the same chunking behavior as vLLM? We rely on early token streaming for UX.
[02:44] Alyssa: Yes, Redwood streaming supports chunked send and function calling. Small caveat — batching can change intra-response timing, but for low-latency mode we can disable batching or use micro-batches.

-- Eval parity approach & benchmarks --
[03:00] Diego: Proposed parity plan: 1) you share your 10k prompt set and scoring harness 2) we run a 24hr parity benchmark across your existing vLLM/TGI baseline and Redwood hosted and Dedicated variants 3) we provide a diff report with score deltas, token counts, latency percentiles, and cost per 1M tokens replicates.
[03:22] Priya: That sounds good. Can you run both hosted and Dedicated in the same run so we can compare ops tradeoffs?
[03:29] Diego: Yep. We'll also run a config with quantized weights (if model supports it) to show cost/latency tradeoffs. We can't always guarantee exact floating-point parity, but the task-level metrics are what matter.
[03:43] Tom: About quantization — our ops team is nervous about quality regressions when going int8. Can you show quality vs. quant curve?
[03:50] Diego: Absolutely. Redwood Optimize will produce recommendation profiles (batch size, quantization level, and kv-cache settings) and show expected delta. We'll surface which prompts are most impacted.

-- Security & compliance --
[04:05] Elena: Key questions: does hosted data leave region, how is KMS handled, can we bring our HSM, audit log retention window, and SSO/SAML support? Also, do you have SOC2 and ISO?
[04:18] Alyssa: Hosted is region-aware; you can restrict to particular cloud regions. For Private and Dedicated, you can integrate with your KMS or use our managed KMS — we support external key wrapping and HSM-backed KMS providers. We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO artifacts; happy to share.
[04:35] Elena: For audit logs we need 12 months retention and immutable logs. Can Redwood provide legally defensible logs?
[04:41] Diego: We have audit log exports and long-term retention add-on. For Private, logs are under your VPC and you can push them to your SIEM. We'll include specifics in the security packet.

-- Cost & SLO tradeoffs --
[04:58] Priya: High level, what are the unit economics? If we move from OpenAI to Redwood hosted, what's typical percent cost reduction (assuming same model family)?
[05:07] Alyssa: It varies by model and token distribution. For gpt-style models we see 10–40% improvements by better batching/caching and intel kernel choices. For Dedicated with reserved capacity, unit cost can drop further. We'll show a model-level cost projection based on your recent token mix.
[05:25] Tom: If we pin to Dedicated, what is the commitment like and how do burst windows work?
[05:29] Alyssa: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with optional burst credits for peak. Commitments are monthly or annual; we'll share typical configs (e.g., 4xA100 dedicated pool) and pricing tiers.

-- Technical deep-dive snippets (Diego) --
[05:45] Diego: A few notes: Redwood's runtime can do continuous batching and KV cache across requests, and we have optimized kernels for FP16 and int8 paths. When you compare vLLM, differences often come from default sampling temperature, top-p, and tokenizer pre/post-processing. We'll align sampling params exactly in parity tests.
[06:05] Priya: Good — we also use custom pre- and post-process hooks in TGI. Can Redwood support server-side transforms?
[06:12] Diego: Yes, function-calling and structured output transforms are supported. You can run transforms in the request path or via a post-processing webhook.
[06:20] Tom: What about model version pinning and rollbacks? We need canary deploys for new weights.
[06:25] Alyssa: Redwood supports model version pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback). The Console gives per-route metrics so you can watch regressions.

-- Risk & edge cases --
[06:40] Priya: One risk is subtle regressions on safety filters and hallucinations. We have finetuned mitigations. How do you recommend validating safety after a migration?
[06:50] Diego: We tie safety checks into evals — run your safety suites, threshold alerts, and sample-based human audits. If issues surface, we can pin to previous model version or adjust sampling.
[07:03] Elena: Legal asked about data residency for EU customers — do you have region-restricted hosting?
[07:09] Alyssa: Yes, hosted in-region options and Private for strict residency. We'll call out region endpoints in the security pack.

-- Objections & clarifications --
[07:24] Tom: How invasive is migration? We have production hooks into OpenAI with streaming and function calls.
[07:29] Diego: We provide SDKs and a compatibility shim that mimics OpenAI endpoints for minimal code change. For streaming semantics and function-calling we map to equivalent behaviors; you'll mostly need to adjust endpoint URLs and test tokenization differences.
[07:46] Priya: Are there customers who ran vLLM -> Redwood and saw better throughput?
[07:52] Alyssa: Yes, we've had a couple — one reduced cost 30% using Dedicated with intelligent caching, another consolidated multiple vendors and simplified ops. We'll anonymize and share those case studies.

-- Agreeing success criteria --
[08:05] Priya: Our success criteria for the pilot: parity within 3% on our scoring suite, p95 latency under 350ms for short prompts, and cost per token at least 10% lower or predictable with Dedicated. If those are met we move to a three-month pilot.
[08:22] Alyssa: That's clear. We'll codify that in the test plan.

-- Logistics & Hands-on items --
[08:30] Alyssa: For the parity run we'll need: your prompt set (10k), expected scoring harness, and a representative traffic trace. Can you provide those?
[08:38] Tom: Yes, we'll sanitize and share a subset by next Wednesday.
[08:43] Priya: Also list of stakeholders for approvals.
[08:46] Elena: We'll need the security docs before we give sensitive data.
[08:50] Alyssa: Understood — I'll send SOC2 + security packet within 48 hours.

-- Closing / Recap --
[09:00] Alyssa: Recap — Redwood will: share security docs, provision parity benchmark for hosted and Dedicated, provide cost projection, and schedule a technical deep dive. LumenArc will: share prompt set, traffic traces, and stakeholder list.
[09:12] Diego: I'll be the technical owner for the benchmark and will request a small sample first to validate harness.
[09:17] Priya: Sounds good. Timeline ok — if we see parity, we can start pilot in September.
[09:22] Elena: Please include audit log retention and KMS integration details in the security packet.
[09:27] Alyssa: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[09:30] Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "kv cash" instead of "kv cache" in some auto-notes). Shared artifacts referenced: security_packet_v1.pdf (link to be sent), parity_benchmark_template.xlsx (to be shared), sample_clientshim_openai_compat (code repo link).

Recap (short): 42m discovery focused on migration parity from vLLM/TGI/OpenAI, tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private, security requirements and a commitment to run a 24h parity benchmark and share security docs.
